**USS _Gerald R. Ford_ (CVN-78)** is an aircraft carrier of the United States Navy and the lead ship of her class. The ship is named after the 38th president of the United States, Gerald Ford, whose World War II naval service included combat duty aboard the light aircraft carrier_Monterey_ in the Pacific Theater.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-16)
Construction began on 11 August 2005, when Northrop Grumman held a ceremonial steel cut for a 15-ton plate that forms part of a side shell unit of the carrier. The keel of _Gerald R. Ford_ was laid down on 14 November 2009. She was christened on 9 November 2013.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-NavyLiveChristening-5)_Gerald R. Ford_ entered the fleet, replacing the decommissioned USS _Enterprise_(CVN-65), which ended her 51 years of active service in December 2012.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-NavyCVN21Issues-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-18)
Originally scheduled for delivery in 2015, _Gerald R. Ford_ was delivered to the Navy on 31 May 2017 and formally commissioned by President Donald Trump on 22 July 2017. She departed Naval Station Norfolk on her first deployment on 2 May 2023. When she was commissioned she was the world's largest aircraft carrier and the largest warship ever constructed.
Ford in his U.S. Navy uniform, c.1945

In 2006, while Gerald Ford was still alive, Senator John Warner of Virginia proposed to amend a 2007 defense-spending bill to declare that CVN-78 "shall be named the USS _Gerald Ford_."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-19) The final version, signed by President George W. Bush on 17 October 2006,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-2007Authorization-20) declared only that it "is the sense of Congress that ... CVN-78 should be named the U.S.S. _Gerald R. Ford_".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-H5122-21) Since such "sense of" language is typically non-binding and does not carry the force of law, the Navy was not required to name the ship after Ford.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-CSPANQuestion-22)

### Performance improvements
These performance enhancements were problematic in Pentagon tests, and final software fixes for some of the problems were delayed until after the ship's post-shakedown availability in 2019.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-TestPhase-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-EMALS-AAG-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-1st_Launch-63)

### Operational and major system testing
[edit]
_Gerald R. Ford_ undergoing the third and final blast of the shock trials, 8 August 2021
In January 2014, the annual Director, Operational Test and Evaluation  report recorded that critical ship systems in laboratory and test environments (including the EMALS, Advanced Arresting Gear, dual-band radar, and weapons elevators) were not reliable enough and needed more testing and improvements. The Navy implemented a rigorous testing program to ensure performance issues would be resolved before the systems were installed on the aircraft carrier._[citation needed_] Major problems with the main turbine generators were found in June 2016.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-64) The fix, requiring design changes, was installed and verified during acceptance trials in May 2017.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-65) The Initial Operational Test & Evaluation milestone was achieved in April 2017.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-66) On 8 April 2017, _Gerald R. Ford_ got underway under her own power for the first time as she headed to sea for builder's trials.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-67) She completed the trials and returned to port at Naval Station Norfolk on 14 April 2017.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-68) On 24 May 2017, she departed for acceptance trials and completed them on 26 May 2017.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-69)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-Delivered-6)

### Operational and major system testing
In 2018, the Navy requested to delay shock trials for at least six years to speed up the ship's deployment, but this request was denied.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-TrialDelay-70) On 18 June 2021, _Gerald R. Ford_ completed her first full-ship shock trial 87 nautical miles (161 km; 100 mi) off Ponce Inlet, Florida, to ensure that she is able to withstand battle conditions.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-72) About 40,000 pounds (18 t) of TNT were detonated underwater, measured as a 3.9 magnitude earthquake by USGS.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-73) Additional tests were conducted in July and August, with the test detonations set off closer to the hull. The ship was determined to have passed the tests, and this concluded the trials.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-ShockTrialsDone-74)

Ford_ in an F/A-18F Super Hornet.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-1st_Launch-63)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-USNIVideo-78)

### Operational and major system testing
According to a GAO report in mid-2020, _Gerald R. Ford_ was still reporting significant problems with the operation of her weapons elevators,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-79) while a DoD report in early 2021 stated that the ship was still not combat ready, citing continuing problems with the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System. Designed to achieve 4,166 aircraft launches between operational mission failures, it instead accomplished only 181.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-81)
On 20 March 2021, _Gerald R. Ford_ and the Italian aircraft carrier _Cavour_ conducted Ready for Operations  by the Italian Navy while transiting the Atlantic Ocean.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-82) In September 2022, Rear Adm. James Downey described the ship as "fully delivered" and has "met her initial operating capability".[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-83)
When she was commissioned, _Gerald R. Ford_ was the world's largest aircraft carrier and the largest warship ever constructed.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-85)

### Operational service
[edit]
_Gerald R. Ford_ returning to Naval Station Norfolk after completing her inaugural deployment to the Atlantic Ocean, 26 November 2022
_Gerald R. Ford_ left Naval Station Norfolk for Task Force Exercise  on 4 October 2022. The carrier was to conduct operations and training exercises alongside NATO allies and partners throughout the Atlantic Ocean. _Gerald R. Ford_'s Carrier Strike Group 12 (CSG 12) included Carrier Air Wing 8, USS _Normandy_, Destroyer Squadron 2 with USS _Ramage_, USS _McFaul_ and USS _Thomas Hudner_, auxiliaries USNS _Joshua Humphreys_ and USNS _Robert E. Peary_, and the United States Coast Guard cutterUSCGC _Hamilton_.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-86) Among the first NATO ships assigned to CSG 12 was the German frigate _Hessen_.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-87)
_Gerald R. Ford_'s first port visit outside of her home country was on 28 October 2022, to Halifax Harbour in Nova Scotia, home of CFB Halifax, Canada's largest military installation and home port of the Royal Canadian Navy's Atlantic fleet.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-90) On 14 November 2022 the ship arrived in United Kingdom waters, for a four-day visit anchored in Stokes Bay near Gosport.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-91) She returned to Norfolk on 26 November 2022.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-92)

### Operational service
USS _Dwight D. Eisenhower_ and USS _Gerald R. Ford_carrier strike groups flank USS _Mount Whitney_, in the Mediterranean Sea, November 2023.
Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin departs USS _Gerald R. Ford_, December 2023
She departed Naval Station Norfolk on her first deployment on 2 May 2023.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-93) On 3 May 2023, _Gerald R. Ford_ departed Naval Station Norfolk on her first full-length deployment and was scheduled to be operating in the 2nd and 6th Fleet's Area of Responsibility.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-94) On 24 May, the ship arrived just outside Oslo, Norway, for NATO exercises,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-96) hosting a visit from Norway's Crown Prince Haakon.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-97) She was scheduled to head towards the Arctic Ocean later for further drills.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-98) On 26 June, the ship sailed to the Mediterranean Sea and arrived at Split, Croatia, for crew rest.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-99) In early October, _Gerald R. Ford_ conducted naval exercises with the Italian navy in the Ionian Sea.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-100)

### Operational service
On 8 October 2023, the day after the Hamas attack on Israel, the U.S. Secretary of Defense, Lloyd Austin, directed the _Gerald R. Ford_ carrier strike group to the eastern Mediterranean "to bolster regional deterrence efforts." Along with the carrier, the group includes the cruiser _Normandy_ and the destroyers _Ramage_, _Carney_, _Roosevelt_, and _Thomas Hudner_.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-101) The U.S. later also sent USS _Dwight D. Eisenhower_-led Carrier Strike Group 2 to the Mediterranean to supplement CSG 12 in the same mission.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-BI-240101-102) While the carrier remained in the Mediterranean, several of her escort ships were sent into the Red Sea, where they repeatedly intercepted missiles and drones fired from Yemen.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-AP-240101-103)

**USS _Gerald R. Ford_ (CVN-78)** is an aircraft carrier of the United States Navy and the lead ship of her class. The ship is named after the 38th president of the United States, Gerald Ford, whose World War II naval service included combat duty aboard the light aircraft carrier_Monterey_ in the Pacific Theater.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-16)
Construction began on 11 August 2005, when Northrop Grumman held a ceremonial steel cut for a 15-ton plate that forms part of a side shell unit of the carrier. The keel of _Gerald R. Ford_ was laid down on 14 November 2009. She was christened on 9 November 2013.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-NavyLiveChristening-5)_Gerald R. Ford_ entered the fleet, replacing the decommissioned USS _Enterprise_(CVN-65), which ended her 51 years of active service in December 2012.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-NavyCVN21Issues-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-18)
Originally scheduled for delivery in 2015, _Gerald R. Ford_ was delivered to the Navy on 31 May 2017 and formally commissioned by President Donald Trump on 22 July 2017. She departed Naval Station Norfolk on her first deployment on 2 May 2023. When she was commissioned she was the world's largest aircraft carrier and the largest warship ever constructed.

texts.3: In 2006, while Gerald Ford was still alive, Senator John Warner of Virginia proposed to amend a 2007 defense-spending bill to declare that CVN-78 "shall be named the USS _Gerald Ford_."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-19) The final version, signed by President George W. Bush on 17 October 2006,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-2007Authorization-20) declared only that it "is the sense of Congress that ... CVN-78 should be named the U.S.S. _Gerald R. Ford_".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-H5122-21) Since such "sense of" language is typically non-binding and does not carry the force of law, the Navy was not required to name the ship after Ford.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-CSPANQuestion-22)

### Operational and major system testing
[edit]
_Gerald R. Ford_ undergoing the third and final blast of the shock trials, 8 August 2021
In January 2014, the annual Director, Operational Test and Evaluation  report recorded that critical ship systems in laboratory and test environments (including the EMALS, Advanced Arresting Gear, dual-band radar, and weapons elevators) were not reliable enough and needed more testing and improvements. The Navy implemented a rigorous testing program to ensure performance issues would be resolved before the systems were installed on the aircraft carrier._[citation needed_] Major problems with the main turbine generators were found in June 2016.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-64) The fix, requiring design changes, was installed and verified during acceptance trials in May 2017.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-65) The Initial Operational Test & Evaluation milestone was achieved in April 2017.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-66) On 8 April 2017, _Gerald R. Ford_ got underway under her own power for the first time as she headed to sea for builder's trials.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-67) She completed the trials and returned to port at Naval Station Norfolk on 14 April 2017.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-68) On 24 May 2017, she departed for acceptance trials and completed them on 26 May 2017.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-69)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-Delivered-6)
texts.13:
### Operational and major system testing
In 2018, the Navy requested to delay shock trials for at least six years to speed up the ship's deployment, but this request was denied.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-TrialDelay-70) On 18 June 2021, _Gerald R. Ford_ completed her first full-ship shock trial 87 nautical miles (161 km; 100 mi) off Ponce Inlet, Florida, to ensure that she is able to withstand battle conditions.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-72) About 40,000 pounds (18 t) of TNT were detonated underwater, measured as a 3.9 magnitude earthquake by USGS.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-73) Additional tests were conducted in July and August, with the test detonations set off closer to the hull. The ship was determined to have passed the tests, and this concluded the trials.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-ShockTrialsDone-74)

### Operational and major system testing
According to a GAO report in mid-2020, _Gerald R. Ford_ was still reporting significant problems with the operation of her weapons elevators,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-79) while a DoD report in early 2021 stated that the ship was still not combat ready, citing continuing problems with the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System. Designed to achieve 4,166 aircraft launches between operational mission failures, it instead accomplished only 181.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-81)
On 20 March 2021, _Gerald R. Ford_ and the Italian aircraft carrier _Cavour_ conducted Ready for Operations  by the Italian Navy while transiting the Atlantic Ocean.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-82) In September 2022, Rear Adm. James Downey described the ship as "fully delivered" and has "met her initial operating capability".[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-83)
When she was commissioned, _Gerald R. Ford_ was the world's largest aircraft carrier and the largest warship ever constructed.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-85)
texts.16:
### Operational service
[edit]
_Gerald R. Ford_ returning to Naval Station Norfolk after completing her inaugural deployment to the Atlantic Ocean, 26 November 2022
_Gerald R. Ford_ left Naval Station Norfolk for Task Force Exercise  on 4 October 2022. The carrier was to conduct operations and training exercises alongside NATO allies and partners throughout the Atlantic Ocean. _Gerald R. Ford_'s Carrier Strike Group 12 (CSG 12) included Carrier Air Wing 8, USS _Normandy_, Destroyer Squadron 2 with USS _Ramage_, USS _McFaul_ and USS _Thomas Hudner_, auxiliaries USNS _Joshua Humphreys_ and USNS _Robert E. Peary_, and the United States Coast Guard cutterUSCGC _Hamilton_.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-86) Among the first NATO ships assigned to CSG 12 was the German frigate _Hessen_.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-87)
_Gerald R. Ford_'s first port visit outside of her home country was on 28 October 2022, to Halifax Harbour in Nova Scotia, home of CFB Halifax, Canada's largest military installation and home port of the Royal Canadian Navy's Atlantic fleet.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-90) On 14 November 2022 the ship arrived in United Kingdom waters, for a four-day visit anchored in Stokes Bay near Gosport.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-91) She returned to Norfolk on 26 November 2022.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-92)

### Operational service
USS _Dwight D. Eisenhower_ and USS _Gerald R. Ford_carrier strike groups flank USS _Mount Whitney_, in the Mediterranean Sea, November 2023.
Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin departs USS _Gerald R. Ford_, December 2023
She departed Naval Station Norfolk on her first deployment on 2 May 2023.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-93) On 3 May 2023, _Gerald R. Ford_ departed Naval Station Norfolk on her first full-length deployment and was scheduled to be operating in the 2nd and 6th Fleet's Area of Responsibility.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-94) On 24 May, the ship arrived just outside Oslo, Norway, for NATO exercises,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-96) hosting a visit from Norway's Crown Prince Haakon.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-97) She was scheduled to head towards the Arctic Ocean later for further drills.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-98) On 26 June, the ship sailed to the Mediterranean Sea and arrived at Split, Croatia, for crew rest.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-99) In early October, _Gerald R. Ford_ conducted naval exercises with the Italian navy in the Ionian Sea.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-100)
texts.18:
### Operational service
On 8 October 2023, the day after the Hamas attack on Israel, the U.S. Secretary of Defense, Lloyd Austin, directed the _Gerald R. Ford_ carrier strike group to the eastern Mediterranean "to bolster regional deterrence efforts." Along with the carrier, the group includes the cruiser _Normandy_ and the destroyers _Ramage_, _Carney_, _Roosevelt_, and _Thomas Hudner_.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-101) The U.S. later also sent USS _Dwight D. Eisenhower_-led Carrier Strike Group 2 to the Mediterranean to supplement CSG 12 in the same mission.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-BI-240101-102) While the carrier remained in the Mediterranean, several of her escort ships were sent into the Red Sea, where they repeatedly intercepted missiles and drones fired from Yemen.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-AP-240101-103)

**USS _Gerald R. Ford_ (CVN-78)** is an aircraft carrier of the United States Navy and the lead ship of her class. The ship is named after the 38th president of the United States, Gerald Ford, whose World War II naval service included combat duty aboard the light aircraft carrier_Monterey_ in the Pacific Theater.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-16)
Construction began on 11 August 2005, when Northrop Grumman held a ceremonial steel cut for a 15-ton plate that forms part of a side shell unit of the carrier. The keel of _Gerald R. Ford_ was laid down on 14 November 2009. She was christened on 9 November 2013.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-NavyLiveChristening-5)_Gerald R. Ford_ entered the fleet, replacing the decommissioned USS _Enterprise_(CVN-65), which ended her 51 years of active service in December 2012.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-NavyCVN21Issues-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-18)
Originally scheduled for delivery in 2015, _Gerald R. Ford_ was delivered to the Navy on 31 May 2017 and formally commissioned by President Donald Trump on 22 July 2017. She departed Naval Station Norfolk on her first deployment on 2 May 2023. When she was commissioned she was the world's largest aircraft carrier and the largest warship ever constructed.

In 2006, while Gerald Ford was still alive, Senator John Warner of Virginia proposed to amend a 2007 defense-spending bill to declare that CVN-78 "shall be named the USS _Gerald Ford_."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-19) The final version, signed by President George W. Bush on 17 October 2006,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-2007Authorization-20) declared only that it "is the sense of Congress that ... CVN-78 should be named the U.S.S. _Gerald R. Ford_".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-H5122-21) Since such "sense of" language is typically non-binding and does not carry the force of law, the Navy was not required to name the ship after Ford.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-CSPANQuestion-22)

### Operational and major system testing
[edit]
_Gerald R. Ford_ undergoing the third and final blast of the shock trials, 8 August 2021
In January 2014, the annual Director, Operational Test and Evaluation  report recorded that critical ship systems in laboratory and test environments (including the EMALS, Advanced Arresting Gear, dual-band radar, and weapons elevators) were not reliable enough and needed more testing and improvements. The Navy implemented a rigorous testing program to ensure performance issues would be resolved before the systems were installed on the aircraft carrier._[citation needed_] Major problems with the main turbine generators were found in June 2016.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-64) The fix, requiring design changes, was installed and verified during acceptance trials in May 2017.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-65) The Initial Operational Test & Evaluation milestone was achieved in April 2017.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-66) On 8 April 2017, _Gerald R. Ford_ got underway under her own power for the first time as she headed to sea for builder's trials.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-67) She completed the trials and returned to port at Naval Station Norfolk on 14 April 2017.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-68) On 24 May 2017, she departed for acceptance trials and completed them on 26 May 2017.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-69)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-Delivered-6)

Ford_ completed her first full-ship shock trial 87 nautical miles (161 km; 100 mi) off Ponce Inlet, Florida, to ensure that she is able to withstand battle conditions.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-72) About 40,000 pounds (18 t) of TNT were detonated underwater, measured as a 3.9 magnitude earthquake by USGS.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-73) Additional tests were conducted in July and August, with the test detonations set off closer to the hull. ### Operational service
[edit]
_Gerald R. Ford_ returning to Naval Station Norfolk after completing her inaugural deployment to the Atlantic Ocean, 26 November 2022
_Gerald R. Ford_ left Naval Station Norfolk for Task Force Exercise  on 4 October 2022. The carrier was to conduct operations and training exercises alongside NATO allies and partners throughout the Atlantic Ocean. _Gerald R. Ford_'s Carrier Strike Group 12 (CSG 12) included Carrier Air Wing 8, USS _Normandy_, Destroyer Squadron 2 with USS _Ramage_, USS _McFaul_ and USS _Thomas Hudner_, auxiliaries USNS _Joshua Humphreys_ and USNS _Robert E. Peary_, and the United States Coast Guard cutterUSCGC _Hamilton_.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-86) Among the first NATO ships assigned to CSG 12 was the German frigate _Hessen_.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-87)
_Gerald R. Ford_'s first port visit outside of her home country was on 28 October 2022, to Halifax Harbour in Nova Scotia, home of CFB Halifax, Canada's largest military installation and home port of the Royal Canadian Navy's Atlantic fleet.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-90) On 14 November 2022 the ship arrived in United Kingdom waters, for a four-day visit anchored in Stokes Bay near Gosport.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-91) She returned to Norfolk on 26 November 2022.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Gerald_R._Ford#cite_note-92)

On 8 October 2023, the day after the Hamas attack on Israel, the U.S. Secretary of Defense, Lloyd Austin, directed the _Gerald R. Ford_ carrier strike group to the eastern Mediterranean "to bolster regional deterrence efforts."
